There is the infants' school nine metres off her on the east and the canal on the
west and the coal road between. There is nowhere for her to go.
So she is to come down by hand, all of her, and everything that comes off her goes
down the inside. Nothing over the side. We are told that is slow and we have

bands.note: Ivy to the first twelve metres, and under it the brick is perfectly sound. The mill has been shut eleven years and nobody has been near her.
Good brick, well laid, and that is the whole difficulty with this job: there is nothing wrong with her. She is coming down because of where she is standing.
Jackdaws in the oversail. They have been there longer than the Council has owned her and they will not be pleased.
Four courses stepping out. The oversail comes off first and it comes off outwards, which is the one place on this job where a dropped brick does not go down the middle.

mission.flueCapacityNote: Everything goes down the inside, because there is a school on one side and a canal on the other. When the flue packs there is no second option — it gets cleared, and that is the afternoon.
